findings.evidence: `grep -rn "smulRange_le_comap" TauCeti --include=*.lean` returns only Module.lean:54 (docstring) and Module.lean:130 (the statement) — no use site. The inline obligation `∀ x ∈ vertexComponent k M v, f x ∈ vertexComponent k N v` is `smulRange_le_comap` read through `Submodule.mem_comap`.
findings.fix: Define `vertexComponentMap k f v := (f.restrictScalars k).restrict (smulRange_le_comap (vertexIdempotent k v) f)`; `vertexComponent k M v` is `smulRange k M (vertexIdempotent k v)` by definition and the file that defines it can unfold it.
findings.issue: `vertexComponentMap` proves its restriction obligation inline (`rw [mem_vertexComponent_iff, ← map_smul f, vertexIdempotent_smul_of_mem_vertexComponent hx]`), re-deriving `TauCeti.smulRange_le_comap` added earlier in the same PR (TauCeti/RingTheory/Idempotents/Module.lean:130). That lemma has no consumer anywhere, despite being advertised in the module docstring as "the pieces are natural in the module".

findings.evidence: Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Projection.lean:650-651; Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/End.lean:269 defines `Module.toModuleEnd R M : S →+* Module.End R M` with `toFun := DistribSMul.toLinearMap R M`, so `Module.toModuleEnd S M e = DistribSMul.toLinearMap S M e` by `rfl`.
findings.fix: `theorem mem_smulRange_iff_smul_eq_self (he : IsIdempotentElem e) : x ∈ smulRange S M e ↔ e • x = x := (he.map (Module.toModuleEnd S M)).mem_range_iff` (`IsIdempotentElem.map` is Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Idempotent.lean:111; `Module.toModuleEnd` is Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LinearMap/End.lean:269 and needs the same `SMulCommClass` instance `DistribSMul.toLinearMap S M e` already uses).
findings.issue: `mem_smulRange_iff_smul_eq_self` re-proves Mathlib's `LinearMap.IsIdempotentElem.mem_range_iff` (Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Projection.lean:650: `{p : M →ₗ[S] M} (hp : IsIdempotentElem p) : x ∈ range p ↔ p x = x`, stated for `[Semiring S] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module S M]`, exactly this generality). Since `smulRange S M e` is by definition `LinearMap.range (DistribSMul.toLinearMap S M e)`, and `Module.toModuleEnd S M e` is that same map, the Mathlib lemma applies verbatim. This is about the proof only, not about deleting the wrapper — the contested round-1 point that `mem_smulRange_iff`/`smul_mem_smulRange` are the only downstream membership API for the unexposed `smulRange` still holds and I am not re-raising it.

findings.evidence: Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Module.lean:429-449 and :465 all use `LinearEquiv.ofBijective (coeLinearMap A) h` directly and supply the simp lemmas for it; the wrapper's only in-file uses are line 241 and line 257.
findings.fix: Delete `smulRangeDirectSumEquiv` and `smulRangeDirectSumEquiv_apply`; state the component lemma directly about `LinearEquiv.ofBijective (DirectSum.coeLinearMap _) (isInternal_smulRange he)`, and prove `finrank_eq_sum_finrank_smulRange` with `rw [← (LinearEquiv.ofBijective _ (isInternal_smulRange he)).finrank_eq, Module.finrank_directSum]`.
findings.issue: `smulRangeDirectSumEquiv` is a thin wrapper for the canonical Mathlib spelling `LinearEquiv.ofBijective (DirectSum.coeLinearMap A) h`, and it drags in a parallel simp API: `smulRangeDirectSumEquiv_apply` (line 229, proved by `rfl`) restates Mathlib's `@[simp] LinearEquiv.ofBijective_apply` (Mathlib/Algebra/Module/Submodule/Equiv.lean:191). Because the wrapper is an unexposed `def`, it also hides Mathlib's `@[simp]` lemmas `DirectSum.IsInternal.ofBijective_coeLinearMap_same` and `_of_ne` from downstream users.

findings.evidence: `grep -rn "vertexIdempotent_smul_mem_vertexComponent" TauCeti --include=*.lean` returns only its own declaration at line 110; the path lemmas use `ofPath_smul_mem_vertexComponent` instead.
findings.fix: Delete it, or use it where the specialization is actually needed.
findings.issue: `vertexIdempotent_smul_mem_vertexComponent` is `smul_mem_smulRange` specialized (its proof is literally `smul_mem_smulRange _ x`) and has no consumer: it is not used in this file, not used anywhere else in the repo, and not listed among the main results in the module docstring. Unlike the round-1 wrappers you defended, this one has no call site to justify the specialization.

summary: The central result (a complete orthogonal family of idempotents decomposes an arbitrary module) is genuinely absent from Mathlib — `grep -rni "orthogonal idempotent" Mathlib` hits only `Mathlib/RingTheory/Idempotents.lean` and `Mathlib/Algebra/DirectSum/Idempotents.lean`, neither of which decomposes a module. But the PR re-derives its own `smulRange_le_comap` in the quiver file, re-proves Mathlib's idempotent range lemma, and adds two wrappers with no consumers.
